correctness.rationale: The four-letter Thue–Morse block 0110/1001 excludes every cyclic length-five palindrome by four explicit starting offsets. Digit-sum decimation gives exact dual palindrome/antipalindrome recurrences at even gaps and an odd-gap antipalindrome radius of 1 or 3. The bases of lengths two and four exhaust the exceptional full axes; valuation descent gives the complete formula, with sharp off-axis maxima checked from length-eight and length-sixteen residue patterns. The two long factors are complements by half-cycle translation. The embedded verifier directly computes all 131056 gap radii at depths 4 through 16, but infinite validity comes from the proof.

originality.rationale: The located classical results cover palindromic complexity, privileged factors and lacunae of the infinite Thue–Morse word; broad circular palindrome counts; and periodicity constraints arising from palindromic word equations. Neither their inspected statements nor identified published mathematical records provide the per-gap radius classification, parity-dependent four maximizers or exact count of long palindromes for each cyclic dyadic iterate. Some plausible full texts remain unavailable, retained as genuine residual risks.

value.rationale: The gap-indexed radius is an exact and naturally motivated local symmetry invariant of cyclic automatic words. Every depth exhibits exactly two macroscopic axes plus four sharp secondary axes; the maximum off-axis palindrome length changes from one quarter to three eighths of the circle with substitution-depth parity. The formula classifies all gap locations and implies an exact two-factor law at every sufficiently long even length, beyond any fixed finite table or routine substitution of a general bound.
